extracted.intended_audience: readers and students of literary biography; scholars interested in Boswell, travel writing, and 18th-century letters
extracted.subtask_description: Criteria and practices for producing and evaluating travel narratives and biographical/journalistic writing, illustrated by James Boswell's Tour in Corsica and his methods as discussed in the essay.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contemporaneous note‑taking / nightly journaling
rubrics_metrics.description: he had written down every night what he had noted during the day, 'throwing together that I might afterwards make a selection at leisure.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Keep daily/contemporaneous notes while traveling (a rough 'throwing together') so you can later select and shape material for publication; preserves freshness and detail for later composition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Veracity in reporting
rubrics_metrics.description: Gray: 'any fool may write a most valuable book by chance, if he will only tell us what he heard and saw _with veracity_.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prioritize truthful, accurate reporting of events and conversations rather than invention or embellishment; readers value authentic accounts of what was actually heard and seen.

rubrics_metrics.name: Novelty of content over exhaustive completeness
rubrics_metrics.description: Johnson's advice: 'you cannot go to the bottom, but all that you tell us will be new.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: It's acceptable not to be exhaustive; aim to present fresh observations or material that will be new to readers rather than attempting impossible comprehensiveness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Style: lightness, delicacy, and pastoral gaiety
rubrics_metrics.description: How admirable is the style of all this, equal quite to Goldsmith's best and lightest touch! Exquisite, too, is that picture... The pathetick simplicity and pastoral gaiety...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adopt an elegant, light-touch prose style for travel scenes and pastoral description—delicacy and genial humour can make reportage pleasing and memorable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authorial orthography / distinctive spelling as authorial voice
rubrics_metrics.description: The peculiar orthography of the writer is defended in the preface, for he allows himself not only such divergencies as 'tremenduous,' 'authour,' 'ambassadour,' but also 'authentick' and 'panegyrick.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authorial spelling or orthographic idiosyncrasies may be consciously defended as part of a writer's voice; such deviations are noted but can be justified by the author in a preface.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assiduous chronicling and self‑promotion
rubrics_metrics.description: He was a most assiduous chronicler of his own actions... there is much Boswell 'copy' buried in the pages of the papers of the time.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Diligent self‑documentation and the use of periodicals/announcements can build reputation and public profile; chronicling one's activities in the press was a deliberate tactic for literary prominence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proactive social engagement / seeking interlocutors
rubrics_metrics.description: The adverse critics have unduly emphasized--his interviewing or forcing himself upon men... 'A man... always makes himself greater as he increases his knowledge.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be willing to press into society and seek out conversations and notable figures; assertiveness in gaining access to sources is defensible because it yields material and increases the writer's knowledge.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of periodicals and pamphlets to rouse public sympathy
rubrics_metrics.description: Mr Boswell took care to keep the newspapers and other publications incessantly warm with various writings, both in prose and in verse, all tending to touch the heart and rouse the parental and sympathetic feelings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Employ newspapers, pamphlets, and literary pieces strategically to influence public opinion or arouse sympathy for a cause; rhetorical appeals to feeling are an explicit tactic.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid affected sublimity and overwrought pathos in lightweight pamphlets
rubrics_metrics.description: The pamphlet ... 'affects the sublime, and some the pathetic; but these are the least tolerable parts of his performance.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In short political or popular pieces, avoid forced attempts at the sublime or excessive pathos—such mannerisms are likely to be judged intolerable by critics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Humour and rollicking gaiety as an asset
rubrics_metrics.description: the rollicking humour of Bozzy in this his first book... 'has pleased and moved me strangely'... The account of Corsica... the rollicking British stage‑tar of tradition...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Energetic humour, songs, and convivial anecdote enliven travel writing and can charm both polite and popular audiences; levity is a recognized virtue in Boswell's mode.

rubrics_metrics.name: Thoroughness and wholehearted commitment to projects
rubrics_metrics.description: He was none of the men that do things by halves...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Approach literary and professional undertakings with zeal and thoroughness rather than half measures; persistent effort yields tangible results (e.g., preparing a book, engaging with prominent figures).
